summary: Deploy dep-0414 (sha 200f96f7, 18:54:00Z) added migration 0007, which dropped the composite index ix_transactions_user_created on transactions(user_id, created_at). Both slow routes filter by user_id and use created_at, so they lost their index. GET /transactions fell from about 13–17 ms to 1.7–3 s, and GET /summary from about 24–35 ms to 1.2–3.2 s. p95 jumped from about 750 ms to about 3150 ms at 18:55Z. Recreate the index (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) or revert the migration. I did not directly confirm the index is missing in the database, and I did not capture a query plan.

root_cause.component: migrations/versions/0007_drop_unused_indexes.py: drop of ix_transactions_user_created on transactions(user_id, created_at)
root_cause.summary: Deploy dep-0414 ran a migration that dropped ix_transactions_user_created, judged 'unused' from idx_scan=0 since the last stats reset. That index serves the per-user queries behind the transaction list (list_recent: WHERE user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT) and the monthly summary (monthly_totals: WHERE user_id AND created_at >= month_start). Without it those queries slowed from tens of milliseconds to seconds, which pushed p95 above 2 s at about 18:55Z, one minute after the deploy.

what_changed.what_changed: The deploy dropped the composite index ix_transactions_user_created (and ix_receipts_content_type) via migration 0007, and removed the Index from the Transaction model.

before.statement: Before the deploy, p95 was about 750 ms (5-minute points of 480–950 ms). GET /transactions took 13–17 ms and GET /summary took 22–35 ms.

after.statement: After the deploy, p95 was about 3150 ms (level shift at 18:55Z). GET /transactions took 1.7–3 s, and GET /summary took 1.2–3.2 s. POST /transactions stayed at 13–16 ms. CPU did not change.

hypotheses.statement: Dropping ix_transactions_user_created in migration 0007 (dep-0414) forced slow queries for the per-user transaction list and monthly summary.

supporting.statement: The deploy landed at 18:54Z and the p95 level shift is at 18:55Z.
The diff removes the index on (user_id, created_at) from the model and drops it in migration 0007.
The two slow routes run queries that filter on user_id and created_at, which this index would serve.
Latency was normal on both routes before the deploy and slow after. Writes (POST /transactions) were unaffected.

contradicting.statement: I did not directly confirm the index is gone in the database and have no query plan. No traces were available.

hypotheses.statement: Resource exhaustion on the single 512 MB web instance (CPU, memory, connections).

contradicting.statement: CPU was flat at 11–18% with no shift. Only the routes that use the dropped index slowed, and request volume did not rise.

hypotheses.statement: A configuration change or traffic increase caused the slowdown.

contradicting.statement: No configuration changes were recorded in the 24 hours before the incident.
Log volume fell slightly against baseline (x0.9) rather than rising.

hypotheses.statement: A downstream dependency (Redis, worker, or an LLM API) is slow.

contradicting.statement: The slow routes are plain database reads. The routes that call other services (/insights, quick-add, /voice/call) are not where the slowdown shows. Error rate is unchanged.

facts.statement: dep-0414 (sha 200f96f7, previous 7bc71c84, message 'migrations: drop indexes with zero scans') went live at 18:54:00Z.
The deploy changed only app/models.py and the new migration 0007_drop_unused_indexes.py.

Migration 0007 drops ix_receipts_content_type and ix_transactions_user_created. Its comment says idx_scan = 0 since the last statistics reset. The model change removes Index('ix_transactions_user_created', user_id, created_at).
p95 shifted from a mean of about 750 ms to about 3154 ms at 18:55Z and stayed high to 19:30Z (peak 3459 ms).
list_recent filters on user_id and orders by created_at desc with a limit. monthly_totals filters on user_id and created_at >= month_start.
Before the deploy, GET /transactions took 13–17 ms and GET /summary took 22–35 ms.
After the deploy, GET /transactions took 1731–3000 ms and GET /summary took 1216–3158 ms. POST /transactions stayed at 13–16 ms.
No configuration changes were recorded in the window, and no past incidents mention indexes.

assumptions: The migration ran successfully at deploy time and the index is actually absent in Neon. This is inferred from the deploy and the matching latency shift, not queried directly.
The slowdown is a sequential or poorly-indexed scan on transactions. No EXPLAIN output or trace spans were available.
idx_scan=0 was probably misleading, for example because pg_stat counters had been reset recently or the stats window was short. This was not verified.
The log lines I sampled are representative of the whole window. The log fetches were partial and capped.

recommended_actions.action: Recreate the index now: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix_transactions_user_created ON transactions (user_id, created_at). Also revert or supersede migration 0007 and the models.py change so the index is not dropped again.
recommended_actions.rationale: This restores the access path used by the transaction list and the monthly summary.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm in Neon that the index is missing (pg_indexes) and run EXPLAIN on the list_recent and monthly_totals queries before and after the fix. Watch p95 return to below 1 s.
recommended_actions.rationale: This closes the gap that the drop was never confirmed directly and no query plan was captured.

recommended_actions.action: Review ix_receipts_content_type as well. Check that no receipts query depends on it, or restore it if one does.
recommended_actions.rationale: It was dropped in the same migration on the same unreliable idx_scan=0 reasoning. Its impact was not examined.

recommended_actions.action: Require evidence beyond idx_scan=0 for index-drop migrations. That means checking how long the stats have been collected, reading the code for queries that use the index, and testing on production-sized data.
recommended_actions.rationale: The index looked unused only because of the stats window, but the code uses it.

missing_evidence: I did not query the database catalog (pg_indexes, pg_stat_user_indexes), so the absence of the index is not directly confirmed. The db_query tool exposes only application tables.
No trace spans were found for the sampled slow request (trace 85d9da041d494513), so I have no per-span timing.
Log fetches were partial and capped, so I could not compute per-route latency statistics.
I did not check why idx_scan was 0, such as when the stats were last reset.
I did not check the impact of dropping ix_receipts_content_type.

changes_considered.change: fivo-api deploy dep-0414, sha 200f96f7: migration 0007 drops ix_transactions_user_created and ix_receipts_content_type, and models.py removes the index
changes_considered.reason: This is the only change in the window. Latency shifted one minute later, and the dropped index matches the filters and ordering of the two slow queries.
